name: OpenLogi
description: ⚡️A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀 — remap buttons, DPI, and SmartShift over HID++. No account, no telemetry.
readmeExcerpt:
> [!WARNING] > **OpenLogi is under active development** and not yet stable — features and config may still change. Give the repo a **Star** ⭐ and **Watch** 👀 it to get notified when a new release lands.

OpenLogi

⚡️ A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀
Unlock the full capabilities of Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over HID++ and UVC

> **Fed up with Options+? Try OpenLogi.** Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. --- ## Beyond Options+ Things OpenLogi does that Options+ won't: - **Stay light.** Native Rust + GPUI. - **Run on Linux.** Linux is a first-class platform in OpenLogi. - **Gestures on supported buttons.** Assign gesture actions to supported controls — or turn gestures off entirely. - **Plain-text config.** Everything is one TOML file you can sync between machines however you like. - **Script it.** A real CLI alongside the GUI: a JSON [automation API](docs/USAGE.md#automation-api) for DPI, SmartShift, Fn-lock, and report rate, plus hardware diagnostics. ## Features

### Devices - Logi Bolt and Unifying receivers, Bluetooth, and wired connections, with battery level and charge state - Low-battery notices at the bottom of the screen, once per discharge, with no OS notification permission - An on-screen indicator when a keyboard turns Caps Lock on or off, plus Num Lock and Scroll Lock on Windows and Linux
Easy-Switch
  • See which computer is paired on each channel, with its OS and connection
  • Rename a channel on devices that allow it
### Buttons and actions
Remap any button
  • A built-in action catalog, custom shortcuts, typed text, or multi-step workflows
  • Separate tap and hold actions, and hold-to-talk chords that release with the button
  • Gestures on Middle Click, Back/Forward, DPI/ModeShift, the gesture button, and the haptic panel
Actions Ring
  • Eight actions in a ring around the cursor
  • Its own layout per application
Keyboard keys
  • Bind media, emoji, screenshot, and other dedicated keys like mouse buttons
  • Restore one key to its device default, or reset the whole row
Per-application profiles switch with the focused app. An `[apps]` alias lets one profile follow an application across platforms. ### Pointer and scrolling
Pointer
  • DPI presets with cycle and set-preset actions
  • Pointer speed and report rate
  • Precision Mode: one button switches the mouse to its slowest speed and back
SmartShift
  • Wheel mode and sensitivity
  • Scrolling force on SmartShift Enhanced mice
  • A permanent-ratchet switch

Scrolling
  • Scroll inversion per device, natively or in software
  • Wheel resolution and smooth wheel scrolling
  • Hold Back or Forward and roll the wheel to scroll sideways on mice without a thumb wheel
### Keyboard and lighting
Keyboard
  • Fn Lock, and multi-platform keyboards that stay on the host OS layout
  • Backlight level, automatic brightness, battery saving, and how long the keys stay lit
  • The backlight level shown on screen as it changes
  • Static RGB on supported keyboards
Litra lights
  • Power, brightness, and color temperature
  • Turns on with the camera if you want
  • Keeps a change made on the light itself
### Webcams - Any Logitech UVC webcam (Brio, StreamCam, the C920 series, …), plug and play - Live preview that holds the camera only while you watch; leave it and the LED goes off - Zoom, pan, tilt, focus, exposure, white balance, and every other UVC control, written to the hardware so Meet, Zoom, and OBS see the change - Built-in Default / Streaming / Video call profiles plus your own snapshots, kept per camera Feature coverage depends on what each device reports; the app shows only the controls a device supports. ### Platform support | Feature | macOS | Windows | Linux | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mouse button remapping and gestures | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Keyboard F-key remapping | ✓ | ✓ | — | | Per-application profiles | ✓ | ✓ | X11, wlroots (sway, Hyprland), GNOME with the [companion extension](crates/openlogi-hook/gnome-shell-extension/README.md) | | Mouse profile follows the window under the pointer | ✓ | ✓ | X11 only | | Media keys | Native | Native | D-Bus MPRIS | | Window-manager actions (desktops, Mission Control, …) | Native | Native equivalents | GNOME, KDE (KWin), Hyprland; some macOS-only actions do nothing | | Menu-bar / tray icon | ✓ | ✓ | — | | In-app updates | Sparkle | Built-in | Built-in | ## Install > [!IMPORTANT] > Quit **Logi Options+** (and Solaar on Linux) first. Only one application can own a receiver at a time. | Platform | System | Architecture | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS | macOS 13 or later | Apple silicon, Intel | | Linux | GLIBC 2.35 or newer | x86_64, arm64 | | Windows | Tested on Windows 11 | x86_64, arm64 | Every download carries a minisign signature and an entry in `SHA256SUMS`. To build from source, see [DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). ### macOS

 

Or with Homebrew: ```sh brew install --cask openlogi ``` Open OpenLogi and grant **Accessibility** and **Input Monitoring** when macOS asks. OpenLogi then updates itself through Sparkle. ### Linux

Warning

OpenLogi is under active development and not yet stable — features and config may still change. Give the repo a Star ⭐ and Watch 👀 it to get notified when a new release lands.

OpenLogi

⚡️ A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀
Unlock the full capabilities of Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over HID++ and UVC

Fed up with Options+? Try OpenLogi.

Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Beyond Options+

Things OpenLogi does that Options+ won't:

  • Stay light. Native Rust + GPUI.
  • Run on Linux. Linux is a first-class platform in OpenLogi.
  • Gestures on supported buttons. Assign gesture actions to supported controls — or turn gestures off entirely.
  • Plain-text config. Everything is one TOML file you can sync between machines however you like.
  • Script it. A real CLI alongside the GUI: a JSON automation API for DPI, SmartShift, Fn-lock, and report rate, plus hardware diagnostics.

Features

Devices

  • Logi Bolt and Unifying receivers, Bluetooth, and wired connections, with battery level and charge state
  • Low-battery notices at the bottom of the screen, once per discharge, with no OS notification permission
  • An on-screen indicator when a keyboard turns Caps Lock on or off, plus Num Lock and Scroll Lock on Windows and Linux
Easy-Switch
  • See which computer is paired on each channel, with its OS and connection
  • Rename a channel on devices that allow it

Buttons and actions

Remap any button
  • A built-in action catalog, custom shortcuts, typed text, or multi-step workflows
  • Separate tap and hold actions, and hold-to-talk chords that release with the button
  • Gestures on Middle Click, Back/Forward, DPI/ModeShift, the gesture button, and the haptic panel
Actions Ring
  • Eight actions in a ring around the cursor
  • Its own layout per application
Keyboard keys
  • Bind media, emoji, screenshot, and other dedicated keys like mouse buttons
  • Restore one key to its device default, or reset the whole row

Per-application profiles switch with the focused app. An [apps] alias lets one profile follow an application across platforms.

Pointer and scrolling

Pointer
  • DPI presets with cycle and set-preset actions
  • Pointer speed and report rate
  • Precision Mode: one button switches the mouse to its slowest speed and back
SmartShift
  • Wheel mode and sensitivity
  • Scrolling force on SmartShift Enhanced mice
  • A permanent-ratchet switch

Scrolling
  • Scroll inversion per device, natively or in software
  • Wheel resolution and smooth wheel scrolling
  • Hold Back or Forward and roll the wheel to scroll sideways on mice without a thumb wheel

Keyboard and lighting

Keyboard
  • Fn Lock, and multi-platform keyboards that stay on the host OS layout
  • Backlight level, automatic brightness, battery saving, and how long the keys stay lit
  • The backlight level shown on screen as it changes
  • Static RGB on supported keyboards
Litra lights
  • Power, brightness, and color temperature
  • Turns on with the camera if you want
  • Keeps a change made on the light itself

Webcams

  • Any Logitech UVC webcam (Brio, StreamCam, the C920 series, …), plug and play
  • Live preview that holds the camera only while you watch; leave it and the LED goes off
  • Zoom, pan, tilt, focus, exposure, white balance, and every other UVC control, written to the hardware so Meet, Zoom, and OBS see the change
  • Built-in Default / Streaming / Video call profiles plus your own snapshots, kept per camera

Feature coverage depends on what each device reports; the app shows only the controls a device supports.

Platform support

Feature macOS Windows Linux
Mouse button remapping and gestures ✓ ✓ ✓
Keyboard F-key remapping ✓ ✓ —
Per-application profiles ✓ ✓ X11, wlroots (sway, Hyprland), GNOME with the companion extension
Mouse profile follows the window under the pointer ✓ ✓ X11 only
Media keys Native Native D-Bus MPRIS
Window-manager actions (desktops, Mission Control, …) Native Native equivalents GNOME, KDE (KWin), Hyprland; some macOS-only actions do nothing
Menu-bar / tray icon ✓ ✓ —
In-app updates Sparkle Built-in Built-in

Install

Important

Quit Logi Options+ (and Solaar on Linux) first. Only one application can own a receiver at a time.

Platform System Architecture
macOS macOS 13 or later Apple silicon, Intel
Linux GLIBC 2.35 or newer x86_64, arm64
Windows Tested on Windows 11 x86_64, arm64

Every download carries a minisign signature and an entry in SHA256SUMS. To build from source, see DEVELOPMENT.md.

macOS

 

Or with Homebrew:

brew install --cask openlogi

Open OpenLogi and grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring when macOS asks. OpenLogi then updates itself through Sparkle.

Linux

   

Or install the right package for your distribution with one command. It verifies the minisign signature and starts the agent; install minisign first:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

On Arch Linux, the openlogi AUR package builds the release from source:

yay -S openlogi

To read the script before running it, and for the AUR package, Flatpak, NixOS, and distributions without systemd, see INSTALL-linux.md.

Windows

 

Usage (CLI)

See USAGE.md

Configuration

Settings use plain TOML; saves preserve symlinked config files. See CONFIGURATION.md.

Developing

See DEVELOPMENT.md, including macOS input-hook safety.

Acknowledgments

  • Windows, cameras, and i18n by @davidbudnick — keyboard RGB, Windows support, Logitech webcam support
  • Linux port by @cserby — Linux support
  • Solaar by @pwr — open-source HID++ implementation
  • Mouser by @TomBadash — a local, account-free Options+ replacement

releases.name: v0.8.16
releases.body:
## macOS: shortcut keys now go through a virtual HID keyboard

When a button sends a keyboard shortcut, OpenLogi now presses the keys on a virtual keyboard named "OpenLogi Virtual Keyboard" instead of posting software key events. macOS handles these keys the way it handles keys from a USB keyboard. This is for shortcuts that work from a real keyboard but did not work from OpenLogi ([#1653](https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/issues/1653), [#744](https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/issues/744)). Apple granted OpenLogi the restricted HID virtual-device entitlement for this, and the signed OpenLogi Agent carries it ([#1918](https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/pull/1918), [#1929](https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/pull/1929)).

- You do not need to grant a new permission. The agent's signing identity did not change, so your Accessibility and Input Monitoring grants keep working.
- If macOS does not let OpenLogi create the virtual keyboard, OpenLogi types the keys the old way.
- Only the signed release builds have it. Builds from source and dev builds still use the old way.
- To check that it is active, run `ioreg -r -c IOHIDUserDevice | grep "OpenLogi Virtual Keyboard"` while Open

aiSummary.oneLiner: A native, lightweight, telemetry-free Rust alternative to Logitech Options+ for peripheral configuration.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenLogi is a high-performance, native application written in Rust that serves as a direct replacement for proprietary Logitech software. It communicates with Logitech mice and keyboards using low-level HID++ protocols, allowing users to remap buttons, adjust DPI, and configure SmartShift functionality without requiring an account or transmitting telemetry. The application avoids heavy web-based frameworks by utilizing a fast GPUI frontend, ensuring a minimal memory footprint. It focuses on privacy and local-first execution, offering power users complete control over their hardware through a reliable, open-source toolchain.
keyFeatures: Low-Level HID++ Control: Communicates directly with peripherals to adjust hardware-level features like DPI and SmartShift.
Telemetry-Free Privacy: Operates entirely locally without requiring user accounts or sending any diagnostic data to remote servers.
Native Rust Implementation: Built from the ground up in Rust for maximum performance and minimal system resource consumption.
GPUI Frontend: Utilizes a fast, native graphical interface rather than relying on heavy, resource-intensive Electron wrappers.
Advanced Button Remapping: Provides comprehensive configuration options to map mouse buttons to custom OS-level actions.

useCases.title: Privacy-Preserving Configuration
useCases.description: Security-conscious users configure their MX Master mouse without installing bloated, telemetry-heavy vendor software.

useCases.title: Performance Optimization
useCases.description: Gamers utilize the native Rust application to manage DPI settings while keeping background resource usage to an absolute minimum.

useCases.title: Hardware Customization
useCases.description: Power users remap specific mouse buttons to trigger complex macros or OS-level shortcuts natively.

useCases.title: SmartShift Tuning
useCases.description: Professionals easily adjust the sensitivity and toggle behavior of the SmartShift scroll wheel directly through the GPUI interface.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and power users seeking a lightweight, private, and highly performant alternative for configuring Logitech peripherals. The platform simplifies complex workflows and accelerates development timelines.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Check the GitHub releases page to download the latest binary for your specific operating system.
